headline: EvilTokens PhaaS compromised over 12,000 mailboxes; Microsoft disrupts AI-powered platform
summary: EvilTokens, a Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platform, abused device code authentication on legitimate Microsoft pages to steal tokens and email data, even bypassing MFA. Microsoft has now disrupted the AI-assisted operation.
details: Developed by Storm-2992, EvilTokens is a Phishing-as-a-Service (PhaaS) platform offering 44 phishing themes and advanced device-code phishing capabilities. This sophisticated operation has successfully compromised over 12,000 mailboxes.

The platform tricks users into approving attacker-initiated sessions on legitimate Microsoft pages. This method allows attackers to steal authentication tokens and email data, effectively bypassing even multi-factor authentication (MFA).

Microsoft recently disrupted this AI-assisted platform, preventing further compromises. The attack highlighted a critical vulnerability in device code authentication flows, even when legitimate Microsoft screens are used.

To mitigate such threats, security experts recommend blocking device code authentication flows by default, making exceptions only for required devices and resource accounts. Correlating lure emails, device code authentication, token exchanges, and email operations within the same session is also crucial for detection.

headline_marked: [[Critical WordPress path traversal vulnerability]] exploited in government data theft, Zyxel CVE-2026-7273 also targeted.
headline: Critical WordPress path traversal vulnerability exploited in government data theft, Zyxel CVE-2026-7273 also targeted.
summary: A suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor is leveraging a critical WordPress vulnerability and a Zyxel CVE to deploy web shells, steal credentials, and intrude into internal SQL databases for government data theft.
details: A sophisticated campaign by a suspected Chinese-speaking threat actor has been observed exploiting a critical WordPress wp2shell vulnerability. This chain leads to web shell deployment, credential theft, and internal SQL database intrusion.

Separately, the same actor is actively exploiting CVE-2026-7273 in Zyxel GS1900 devices. This highlights a multi-faceted breach path targeting public web servers, network devices, credentials, and internal databases.

Organizations are urged not to treat this as merely patching a single product vulnerability. Instead, it must be handled as a coordinated incident requiring investigation into web shells, unauthorized accounts, SQL authentication, and data exfiltration alongside patching.
